answers.value: Population = every demand item in Jira project 'DEMAND' with status 'Triage' and label 'funding-check-pending'; funding validated against the approved FY capital/opex plan line in the PPM tool (Clarity), capacity validated against the current PI capacity plan for the owning squad.
Current fiscal quarter plus the next quarter (rolling 6-month planning horizon); funding effective date must fall within the approved FY budget period.
Demand record has non-null Funding Source, Approved Budget Amount (>0), Cost Center, Target PI, and Assigned Squad; funding amount and squad capacity in story points are both populated and > 0.
Sum of committed demand for the target PI reconciles to the squad's available capacity in Jira Align within +/- 5%; funding drawn reconciles to the Clarity plan line remaining balance to the dollar.
Funding/capacity confirmation comment posted to the Jira demand item with author, ISO-8601 timestamp, and Clarity plan line ID; Jira issue history version retained per Jira audit log (immutable).
Items failing the funding or capacity check are moved to Jira status 'Blocked-Funding' with a comment stating the gap; disposition tracked to closure by the Product Owner within 5 business days.
All demand items that entered status 'Triage' in the in-scope quarter (100% inspection, not a sample — typical volume 40-80 items/quarter).

PASS = both funding (Clarity plan line with remaining balance >= approved amount) and capacity (squad points available >= estimate) confirmed and recorded; FAIL if either is missing. Target: 100% of items progressed to analysis have a recorded funding+capacity confirmation; 0 exceptions.

On FAIL, re-perform the check against Clarity and Jira Align; if still failing, raise a Jira ticket type 'SDLC-Exception' assigned to the Engineering Manager with a 10-business-day remediation SLA and hold the item in 'Blocked-Funding'.
Confirmations dated within the current PI; funding effective within the approved FY budget window.

Acceptance = a Jira comment on the demand item recording confirmed funding source + Clarity plan line ID and confirmed squad capacity in points, authored by the Product Owner. Evidence lives on the Jira demand item (comment + issue history) and the Clarity plan line; link both in the demand item's 'Evidence' field.

Score, rationale, and scorer recorded in Jira custom fields with issue-history timestamp; scoring session notes retained in Confluence with version and date.

answers.value: Population = all active demand items in the Jira 'DEMAND' backlog register (statuses New/Triage/Analysis/Blocked); the register is the saved Jira board 'Demand Pipeline' plus its Confluence-embedded roll-up.
Live register; each item's status/priority/owner must have been touched within the last 10 business days or flagged stale.
Every register row has non-null Status, Priority (P1-P4), Assigned Owner, and Last-Updated date; no item in 'Analysis' older than 30 days without a status update.
Register item count reconciles to the Jira 'DEMAND' project open-issue count exactly (delta = 0); reconciliation run weekly via saved JQL export.
Weekly register snapshot exported to the compliance evidence repository (CSV + PDF) with export timestamp and generating user; prior snapshots retained 12 months.
Stale items (>10 business days untouched) auto-flagged 'register-stale'; owner must update or re-triage within 3 business days, disposition logged in the item comment.
All open items on the Demand Pipeline board at the weekly reconciliation cut (100% inspection).
PASS = 100% of open items have Status, Priority, and Owner populated and Last-Updated within SLA; FAIL if any mandatory field null or >5% of items stale. Threshold: <=5% stale tolerated with waivers.

Source-system control total: Jira REST count endpoint for project=DEMAND AND statusCategory!=Done, compared to the register export row count.

Authorized approver = Product Owner (register owner) per the RACI on the Confluence 'Demand Governance' page; delegation to the Scrum Master permitted during PO absence, recorded in the delegation log with start/end dates.

answers.value: Population = all approved business needs/features for the release under analysis mapped to their derived user stories; RTM covers 100% of in-scope features in the Jira Align capability plus their child stories in Jira.
The current release/PI increment; RTM baselined at design sign-off and re-verified at code-complete.
Each RTM row links Business Need ID -> Requirement/Feature -> User Story (Jira key) -> Test Case (Jira/Zephyr key), all four columns non-null; acceptance criteria present on every story.

Count of features in the RTM equals count of features in the Jira Align release; every story in the release appears exactly once (no orphan stories, no unmapped needs) — bidirectional trace delta = 0.
RTM exported to Confluence and the source repo /docs as a versioned artifact tagged with the release version and generation timestamp; commit SHA recorded.
Requirements with no downstream story, or stories with no upstream need, are logged as RTM gaps in Jira and dispositioned (add story / descope / waiver) by the BA within one sprint.
RTM methodology = bidirectional traceability template v2.1 approved by the BA Chapter; version recorded in the RTM header.
Sensitivity: any change to a business need or scope item must trigger an RTM diff review; threshold = >3 unmapped rows blocks release readiness sign-off.
Materiality: RTM completeness must be >=98% (mapped rows / total rows); below 95% is a release blocker.
All requirement/story/test rows in the RTM for the release (100% inspection).
PASS = every requirement traces to >=1 story and >=1 test case, and every story traces to >=1 requirement; coverage >=98%. FAIL if any requirement or story is orphaned beyond the 2% tolerance.

On FAIL, list orphaned rows and assign remediation to the BA; unresolved gaps at release gate raise a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' to the Product Owner with a 10-business-day SLA and explicit descope/waiver decision.
Field definitions: Jira Align 'Feature', Jira 'Story' and 'Acceptance Criteria' field, Zephyr 'Test Case' — as defined in the tool field configurations for the release board.
Control total: Jira Align feature count and Jira story count for the release fix-version, cross-checked against RTM row counts.

Acceptance = RTM shows 100% bidirectional trace (need<->story<->test) at >=98% completeness and is reviewed by the Test Lead. Evidence = versioned RTM in Confluence + source repo /docs, linked from the release readiness page.

checklist.step: Trace every requirement to its work item
checklist.value: RTM binds each business need to a Jira story key and test case key.

testing.value: Requirements with zero linked stories = 0.

Prior quarter's completed deliveries; lessons captured within 10 business days of go-live.
Each lessons-learned record has non-null What-Went-Well, What-To-Improve, Root Cause, and >=1 Action Item with an owner and due date; action items created as Jira tickets labeled 'lessons-learned'.
Count of retrospective records equals count of completed deliveries for the quarter (100% coverage); reconcile Confluence page count to Jira released fix-versions.
Each retro page is versioned in Confluence with author and date; action-item Jira tickets carry created-date and link back to the retro page.
Deliveries with no retro within 10 business days flagged; Scrum Master schedules a catch-up retro within one sprint and records the exception reason.

checklist.step: Run knowledge-sharing on captured lessons
checklist.value: Top improvement themes each quarter are presented in the weekly engineering knowledge-sharing session; slides stored in Confluence.

testing.value: At least one knowledge-sharing session per quarter references the quarter's lessons-learned; check session log.

checklist.value: Retro pages added within 10 business days of each go-live; index page kept up to date.

answers.value: Population = all backlog items proposed for the upcoming sprint/PI in Jira project 'DEMAND'/team backlog; dependency analysis covers technical, data, team, and external-vendor dependencies for each candidate story.
The sprint or PI immediately prior to commitment; re-run at PI planning and again at sprint planning.

Each candidate story has its 'blocks/is-blocked-by' Jira links evaluated; CMDB CI dependencies checked for impacted services; every identified blocker recorded as a Jira 'Depends On' link with target date and owning team.
Number of stories reviewed equals number of committed candidates (100%); count of open blocking links reconciles to the sprint dependency board.
Dependency map exported from Jira and stored in Confluence with sprint/PI tag and timestamp; CMDB queries retained with run date.
Stories with unresolved hard blockers are pulled from the sprint commitment and labeled 'blocked-external'; Scrum Master tracks each to resolution or descope, disposition noted per item.
All stories proposed for the sprint/PI commitment (100% inspection).

PASS = every committed story has its dependencies identified and each hard blocker has a target resolution date <= sprint start; FAIL if any committed story carries an unmanaged open blocker. Threshold: 0 committed stories with unresolved hard dependencies.

On FAIL, remove the blocked story from commitment or negotiate the dependency date; if a cross-team blocker cannot be dated, raise a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' to the Release Train Engineer with a 10-business-day SLA.
Acceptance criteria: no committed story enters the sprint with an open, undated is-blocked-by link; all identified blockers have owner + target date.
Evidence location: Jira dependency links on each story + the Confluence dependency map page for the sprint/PI, linked from the sprint planning notes.

checklist.step: Record dependencies as work-item links
checklist.value: Blockers captured as Jira 'is-blocked-by' links on the story, not in prose.

testing.value: Committed stories with a known blocker but no Jira dependency link = 0.

answers.value: Population = all test execution results for the release under test — unit, integration, system, regression, and UAT — pulled from Zephyr/Jira and the CI pipeline for the release fix-version; report covers 100% of executed test suites plus open defects.
The current release test cycle, from test-cycle open to code-freeze/go/no-go gate.

Report has non-null Tests Planned/Executed/Passed/Failed/Blocked, Pass Rate, Coverage %, Open Defects by severity (S1-S4), and Outstanding Risk items with owners; each metric sourced from a named query.
Executed = Passed + Failed + Blocked (arithmetic reconciles); reported defect counts reconcile to Jira defect JQL for the fix-version; coverage % matches the CI/SonarQube report — all deltas = 0.
Signed test summary report (PDF) stored in the compliance evidence repository with release version, generation timestamp, and CI build number; underlying Zephyr export retained alongside.

Every S1/S2 defect open at report time is listed with a disposition (fix-before-release / deferred-with-waiver / accepted-risk) and an approver; deferrals require a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' with justification.
All test cases and defects associated with the release fix-version (100% inspection).
Release exit criteria: pass rate >=95% on planned tests, 0 open S1, 0 open S2 (or waived), regression suite 100% executed, coverage >=80% on changed lines. FAIL = any exit criterion unmet.

On FAIL, report a no-go recommendation; each unmet criterion gets a remediation owner and a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' (owner = Engineering Manager, 10-business-day SLA) before any conditional go decision.
Field definitions: Zephyr test statuses (Pass/Fail/Blocked/Not Executed), Jira defect Severity scheme (S1-S4), SonarQube coverage metric — per the QA tool configuration for the release board.
Control totals: Zephyr executed-test count and Jira defect count for the fix-version, cross-checked against the report's summary tables.

Acceptance = report shows pass rate >=95%, 0 open S1/S2 (or waived), regression 100% executed, coverage >=80% on changed lines, and is signed by the Test Lead. Evidence = signed PDF in the compliance evidence repository + Zephyr export, linked from the release readiness page.

testing.value: Report contains separate pass/fail figures for each test layer.

answers.value: Population = all non-functional requirements (performance, security, availability, scalability, recoverability) defined for the release; each NFR is reviewed for compliance against its measured/target threshold before the design-assurance gate.
The current release/milestone; NFR compliance assessed at design assurance and re-verified against pre-prod load/security test results.
Each NFR row has non-null Category, Target (with number/unit, e.g. p95 latency <=300ms, availability >=99.9%), Measured Value, Source-of-Measurement, and Status (Met/Not Met/Waived).
Count of NFRs assessed equals count of NFRs defined for the release (100%); measured values reconcile to their evidence source (load test report, SAST/DAST report, availability SLO dashboard).
NFR compliance assessment recorded in the GRC platform with release version, assessor, and timestamp; each measured value linked to its dated test/scan report artifact.

Each 'Not Met' NFR is logged as a GRC finding with severity, remediation owner, and target date; production go requires either remediation or a risk-accepted waiver signed by the CISO (security) or accountable exec.

Policy citations: internal NFR/Architecture Standard (performance, availability tiers) and the Secure SDLC policy; for security NFRs cite NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500.05 (pen testing/vuln mgmt) and 500.15 (secure development).
Retention: NFR assessment records and supporting test/scan reports retained 5 years in the GRC platform per audit policy.
The NFR compliance assessment must be completed and signed before the release go/no-go gate date recorded on the release plan; late assessment blocks the gate.
Pre/post comparison: measured NFR values from the release candidate compared to the prior production baseline; no regression beyond agreed tolerance (e.g. latency not worse than baseline +10%).
Change ticket: linked ServiceNow change record for the release; the NFR sign-off is attached to the change as a gate approval.
All defined NFRs for the release (100% inspection).

PASS = every NFR Met against its numeric target or covered by a signed waiver; e.g. p95 latency <=300ms, availability >=99.9%, 0 critical/high SAST/DAST findings, load test at 1.5x peak sustained. FAIL = any unmet NFR without a waiver.

On FAIL, raise a GRC finding and a Jira 'SDLC-Exception'; security NFR failures route to the Application Security Lead/CISO for risk acceptance, others to the Solutions Architect, 10-business-day remediation SLA.
Acceptance criteria: 100% of NFRs assessed with Met/Waived status, all measured values evidenced, no open critical security NFR, sign-off before the go/no-go gate.
Evidence location: GRC platform NFR assessment record + linked load test report, SAST/DAST scan reports, and SLO dashboard export, referenced from the ServiceNow change record.

Applicable citations: internal Architecture/NFR Standard and Secure SDLC policy; NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500.05 (annual penetration testing / vulnerability management) and 500.15 (secure application development) for the security and availability NFRs.

answers.value: Population = the release/milestone under design assurance; scoping covers which components, integrations, NFRs, security controls, and standards will be reviewed, plus review depth and participants.
The current release/milestone design phase; scope defined before design sign-off and baselined for the review cycle.

Review scope document has non-null In-Scope Components, Out-of-Scope items, Review Criteria/checklist reference, Participants (incl. an independent reviewer), Timeline, and Gate Date; risk-based rationale for depth included.
In-scope component list reconciles to the solution architecture inventory / CMDB CIs for the release (no component silently excluded); count delta = 0 or each exclusion has a stated reason.
Scope/plan document stored in the GRC platform with release version, author, and timestamp; version-controlled and linked from the release readiness page.
Components proposed for exclusion require a documented risk rationale approved by the Enterprise Architect; unjustified exclusions logged as a GRC finding and resolved before review start.
Scope compared to the prior similar release's assurance scope to ensure no control area regressed out of coverage; deltas justified.
Change ticket: linked ServiceNow change record for the release; the design-assurance scope is attached as the review plan.
All components/controls proposed for the review scope (100% inspection of the scope list).

PASS = scope document complete (all mandatory sections populated), an independent reviewer named, and 100% of release components either in-scope or explicitly justified-out; FAIL if any component is silently omitted or no independent reviewer assigned.

On FAIL, complete the missing scope sections or add the independent reviewer before review start; unresolved scoping gaps raise a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' to the Enterprise Architect, 10-business-day SLA.
Acceptance criteria: scope/plan approved with in/out lists, criteria reference, independent reviewer, and gate date before the review kicks off.
Evidence location: GRC platform design-assurance scope record, linked from the release readiness page and the ServiceNow change record.

answers.value: Population = all findings from the design-assurance review for the release — deviations from standards/patterns, architecture/security risks, and recommended remediations; every observation raised during the review is captured.
The current review cycle; findings documented within 5 business days of the review session and before the go/no-go gate.
Each finding record has non-null Description, Standard/Pattern Deviated, Severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low), Risk, Recommended Remediation, Owner, and Target Date; no finding without an owner.
Count of documented findings reconciles to the review meeting minutes / raised-issues list (no finding dropped); GRC finding count matches the review log exactly.
Findings logged in the GRC platform with review ID, author, and timestamp; each finding version-tracked and linked to the review scope record.

Each finding carries a disposition (remediate / accept-risk / defer); risk acceptances require sign-off by the accountable owner (CISO for security), deferrals require a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' with justification.
Findings checked against the prior review's open items to confirm no recurring deviation is re-introduced (pre/post comparison of the deviation register).
Change ticket: linked ServiceNow change record for the release; findings and their dispositions attached as the review outcome.
